fatal_errors: The proposed acid-etching and annealing intervention is unrelated to the target closed-loop, high-throughput composition-and-synthesis discovery campaign.

The claimed Pt-rich protective shell mechanism conflicts with the target mechanism of ageing-induced electronic reconstruction, particularly cooperative Cu–Pt adsorption sites and process-dependent alloy/support interfaces.

The cited evidence concerns electrocatalytic oxygen reduction or alkaline water dissociation rather than supported automotive exhaust catalysis under NO, CO, hydrocarbon, water, and severe thermal-ageing conditions.
No evidence establishes that a Pt-rich shell resists H2O/NO poisoning or improves three-way-catalyst light-off after 900 °C lean/rich ageing.
The hypothesis omits the Pd benchmark, post-ageing optimization criterion, specified synthesis window, multicomponent exhaust feed, and species-resolved performance thresholds central to the target.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad challenge of improving a low-PGM multielement catalyst under exhaust ageing, but reconstructs neither the intervention nor the operative mechanism. Its core-shell proposal is extrapolated from electrochemical HEA literature without evidence that it transfers to supported gasoline-exhaust catalysis. The untreated control, XPS/STEM characterization, and paired ageing test provide some experimental discriminability, but the exhaust conditions and activity metrics are vague, the 15–20% falsification threshold is arbitrary, and there is no comparison with the relevant Pd or random-discovery baselines. Thus it is a conceivable materials idea, but it is not adequately supported for the stated application and does not recover the hidden paper.
